subject_session: identifier not printed; single session, ~1579.8 s, 50 Hz, first 30 units with >100 spikes

justification.dataset: Grid cells are an intrinsically 2D hexagonal phenomenon and cannot be cleanly isolated on a 1D linear track, so the demonstration substrate is wrong regardless of whether 000053 contains MEC units.
justification.handling: Real NWB data was streamed correctly and positions interpolated, but unit selection is just the first 30 cells with >100 spikes with no quality or region criteria.
justification.analysis: The method never performs a grid-cell test (no 2D rate map, no spatial autocorrelogram, no gridness score); it counts peaks in a 1D map and thresholds an invented FFT ratio at the 60th percentile, which cannot identify grid cells.
justification.correctness: Reported values reproduce and are mutually consistent with the figures, but the headline 'clear separation' is guaranteed by construction (top-40% selection on the same metrics), making the statistic circular.
justification.figures: Example maps do not show grid periodicity and the power-spectrum panel shows the labeled grid cell with no spectral peak while the non-grid cell has one, so the figures do not show what the text claims.
justification.honesty: The write-up presents non-grid, broad-field units as reliably identified grid cells and claims strong spectral periodicity that its own spectrum figure contradicts, with no caveat, which caps honesty at 1.
justification.verdict: The phenomenon is not tested or demonstrated and the positive claim is unsupported and contradicted by the run's own figures, so this must start over.
